renderings.value: Indicates contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'although', 'but'.

「～ものの」 is used to connect two parts of a sentence where the first part is true, yet the second part shows a contrasting or unexpected outcome. It can be translated as 'although', 'even though', or 'but still'.
Verb-casual + ものの, い-Adjective + ものの, な-Adjective + なものの, Noun + であるものの
Formal, written register - common in essays and news reporting; rare in casual speech.
Even though I got up early, I didn't catch the bus in time.
Although this room is spacious, there isn't much furniture.
She is beautiful, but her personality is bad.
Although he is a famous singer, not many people came to his concert.
